title: Model-designed mutation paths switched WW-domain binding specificity
summary: The first public preprint appeared on bioRxiv on 2025-12-10. Its reviewed version reports that designed WW-domain mutational paths largely retained binding, while the same mutations introduced in scrambled order disrupted function. The eLife reviewed-preprint v1 (2026-04-09) later quantified binding for 54 of 58 tested designs and described cross-reactive intermediates on some specificity transitions. In-vitro binding to representative peptides does not establish in-vivo function or generalize to all WW domains.
organization: ESPCI Paris; École Normale Supérieure; Sorbonne Université; Université Paris-Saclay; CNRS; CEA

evidence.tested: The primary version history identifies a bioRxiv preprint posted 2025-12-10 before the eLife reviewed-preprint v1 dated 2026-04-09. The eLife v1 reports that 54 of 58 tested sequences designed along model-sampled WW-domain paths bound at least one representative peptide class; variants with the same mutations in scrambled order were nonfunctional. The specific 54/58 count is attributed to the eLife v1, not assumed for the earlier version.
evidence.unknown: In-vitro binding to representative peptides does not establish in-vivo function or generalize to all WW domains.
evidence.ai_role: The learned sequence model sampled intermediate sequences and mutation orders between natural WW domains with different binding specificities.

source_review.scope: Read the eLife reviewed-preprint v1 Methods and Results and version history; checked the version history identifying the earlier 2025-12-10 bioRxiv preprint and author affiliations on the eLife article information page.
